summary: The structure of a web page, building an interface with HTML and CSS, and creating HTML forms for data entry.

blocks.content: Every HTML document has the same skeleton. The `<head>` holds information **about** the page; the `<body>` holds what the user **sees**.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>My School Club</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
<body>
  <header> … </header>
  <nav> … </nav>
  <main> … </main>
  <footer> … </footer>
</body>
</html>

blocks.content: Semantic elements (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `footer`) make the page easier to read for people, **search engines** and **screen readers** — a common "explain why" answer.

theory.title: Creating an interface with HTML and CSS

blocks.content: HTML gives the page its **structure and content**; CSS controls its **appearance**: colours, fonts, spacing and layout.

blocks.content: Every element is a box made of **content**, **padding** (space inside the border), **border** and **margin** (space outside).

blocks.title: The box model
blocks.css:
.box { width: 160px; padding: 20px; border: 4px solid #1f4fd8; margin: 24px; background: #e8eefc; text-align: center; font-family: Arial; }
body { background: #fdf3e2; margin: 0; }

items: **Consistency:** the same colours, fonts and navigation on every page.
**Readability:** good contrast, readable font size, short paragraphs.
**Clear navigation:** the user always knows where they are and how to go back.
**Accessibility:** `alt` text for images, labels for form fields, keyboard access.
**Responsive design:** the layout adapts to phones and computers.
